name: A Canaan Valley lot
blurb: A rural lot at 3,200 feet in West Virginia's Canaan Valley, the highest sizable valley east of the Mississippi: wet meadow, shrub swamp and bog around a blackwater stream, planted red spruce on the slopes above. Dark-eyed juncos work the seed heads in winter, resident birds hold the thickets, deer cross the meadow at dusk, and the seeps keep salamanders and newts in the damp ground.

facts.text: Canaan Valley is the highest sizable valley east of the Mississippi River, with an average valley floor elevation of 3,200 feet (980 m).

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The valley holds 8,400 acres or so of shrub swamp and bog, about 40% of all the wetland in West Virginia and the second largest inland wetland area in the United States.

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The National Park Service called the valley "a splendid 'museum' of Pleistocene habitats ... unique as a northern boreal relict community at this latitude by virtue of its size, elevation and diversity."

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley, quoting the National Park Service citation for its 1974 National Natural Landmark designation
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: A once dense climax forest of red spruce, intermixed with balsam fir and hardwoods, covered the valley a hundred years ago; it was cut between 1888 and 1922 and later replanted with spruce on the slopes.

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The high elevation gives Canaan Valley a growing season of only about 95 days, and it averages 170.2 inches (432 cm) of snow a year.

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The valley and surrounding highlands hold some of the most southerly pockets of snowshoe hare habitat in the species' range.

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Large groups of white-tailed deer are often visible from the valley's main roads, and the animals have become conditioned to people and are no longer frightened by them.

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Davis, in the northern part of the valley, has a warm-summer humid continental climate (Köppen Dfb) and is the highest town in West Virginia, at 3,520 feet.

source.title: Wikipedia: Davis, West Virginia
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Davis, West Virginia", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Almost 70% of the valley has been the Canaan Valley National Wildlife Refuge since 1994, the nation's 500th, and it was designated a National Natural Landmark in 1974.

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: More than 280 animal species and over 580 plant species have been documented in the valley, including mosses, sedges, heathers, large cranberry and Canadian blueberry.

source.title: Wikipedia: Canaan Valley
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Canaan Valley", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
